If you've been missing the Digital Crown double-click feature that used to bring up the app switcher on Apple Watch before watchOS 27, it looks like that functionality is set to return in watchOS 27.2 beta 2. Here are the details.

Apple is working to bring back the watchOS app switcher

Apple rolled out watchOS 27.2 beta 2 to developers earlier today, less than a week after first releasing beta 1.

This beta contains a piece of news that will likely please long-time Apple Watch users, including my colleague Zac Hall. He wrote earlier this month about how watchOS 27 removed the ability to quickly switch between recently used apps by double-clicking the Digital Crown.

In his article, he pointed out that there's currently no way to quickly jump between recent apps, and he hoped Apple would restore this gesture either before the official launch of watchOS 27 or in a future update.

While Apple hasn't restored the Digital Crown app switcher shortcut in this watchOS 27.2 beta 2, it has brought back the app switcher with a new gesture.

According to a discovery in the Apple Den Discord server, shared by user Bones on X, watchOS 27.2 beta 2 lets users bring up the app switcher by long-pressing the bottom of the screen within an app.

As Bones noted in the tweet, the app switcher largely works as it did before: after a long-press at the bottom of the screen activates the app switcher, users can rotate the Digital Crown to scroll through recently used apps, or swipe left on an app and tap the "X" button to remove it from the switcher.

As with all betas, this particular implementation may not necessarily make it to the final release (expected next month), but the addition of this feature in watchOS 27.2 beta 2 shows that Apple is listening to user feedback and working to bring the app switcher back.

Have you been missing the app switcher on watchOS 27? Let us know in the comments.
